ghs.en: She had promptly taken over the President's role from when she was in Second Year.

ghs.remedy: She took over as president early, while she was still a second-year.

highlights.text: She had promptly taken over the President's role from when she was in Second Year.

ghs.en: Our carefree Third Years went to retire shortly afterwards.
ghs.assessment: The senior students wanted to retire as soon as possible, which explains the early handover. The English says they actually proceeded to retire shortly after some unstated event, losing desire and causality.
ghs.remedy: The easygoing third-years had wanted to retire as quickly as possible.

highlights.text: Taichi, but you're a club member... you just have to come by every day!

highlights.text: Until I have that dream, about silly innocent club activities,

highlights.text: about an ordinary life as if ordinary students.

highlights.text: Memories of being as a person.

rows.jp: そして戦いは。

highlights.text: I ended to dive into a Recollection Scene.

rows.jp: 『ＲＧだｚＱＫＩ―――』

ghs.en: 『Tekuimi I lohiishi nrana---』

rows.jp: 『ＲきだっＱＫに―――』

ghs.en: 『Tekuen I lohiishi you---』

rows.jp: 『好きだったのに―――』

ghs.en: 『When I loved you---』
ghs.assessment: 好きだったのに means 'even though I loved you' or 'I loved you, and yet,' with のに carrying an essential frustrated contrast. The English changes it into a neutral temporal clause and omits the concessive relation.
ghs.remedy: Even though I loved you—

highlights.text: When I loved you---

rows.jp: 両手で作った器に、その美しい言葉は、砂漠の水のようにきらめいた。
rows.en: In the bowl of my cupped hands, those beautiful words shimmered like water in the desert.

ghs.en: In these hands of mine that I'd shaped into a bowl these beautiful words glittered and sparkled like water in the desert.

rows.jp: 「俺を……好き？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "You loved... me?"

rows.jp: 声がひりつく。

ghs.en: Speaking smarts.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that his voice feels raw, stinging, or rasping as he speaks. The English makes the abstract act of speaking the body part that hurts.
ghs.remedy: My voice stings.

highlights.text: Speaking smarts.

rows.jp: 「こんな……俺を？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "This... me here?"
ghs.assessment: こんな俺 means 'someone like me' with self-deprecating force. The English treats himself as a demonstrative object located 'here' and never forms a natural question.
ghs.remedy: Someone... like me?

highlights.text: This... me here?

rows.jp: 「ああ……ああ……嬉しい……嬉しいな……」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ahhh... ahhh... so happy... I'm so happy..."

rows.jp: 嬉しい。

ghs.en: I'm so happy.

rows.jp: 夢なら覚めないで……いや、むしろ覚めてくれ。
rows.en: If this was a dream, don’t let me wake… No. Actually, wake me. Please.

ghs.en: Don't wake me if it's a dream... no, rather, wake me.

rows.jp: 世界はこんなに嬉しいのだから。
rows.en: Because there was this much happiness in the world.

ghs.en: Because the world's making me this much happy.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that the world feels or is this joyful, which motivates wanting to wake into it. The English makes the world a causal agent acting on him and uses the nonidiomatic degree phrase 'this much happy.'
ghs.remedy: the world is this full of joy

highlights.text: the world's making me this much happy

rows.jp: また何でもない毎日を、続ける喜びがあるのだから。
rows.en: Because there was joy in going on, one ordinary day after another.

ghs.en: Because I now have the joy to persevere in this daily life of perfect normality again.
ghs.assessment: The source celebrates continuing ordinary, uneventful days again. 'Persevere' adds arduous endurance, 'perfect normality' overstates 何でもない, and English takes joy 'in' continuing rather than 'to' persevere.
ghs.remedy: the joy of continuing ordinary, uneventful days again

highlights.text: the joy to persevere in this daily life of perfect normality again

rows.jp: 次はもうちょっとうまくやれると思うから。
rows.en: Because I thought I could do a little better next time.

ghs.en: As I think I should be able to make things go well next,
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that next time he thinks he can handle things a little better. The English omits 'time' after 'next' and uses the causative phrase 'make things go well' instead of his own performance.
ghs.remedy: do a little better next time

highlights.text: make things go well next

rows.jp: 繰り返したい。
rows.en: I wanted to do it all over again.

ghs.en: I want to do this all over again.

rows.jp: 転生するなら次は『たにし』になって何も考えずに暮らそうと考えもしたが、また人間になってもいいかなあと思う。
rows.en: I had once thought that, if I ever got reincarnated, I’d come back as a pond snail and live without thinking about a thing. But maybe being human again wouldn’t be so bad.

ghs.en: And so even if I had this idea of wanting to reincarnate into a pond snail and live my life without having anything to think about at all, maybe it would just be nice if I were to be a human again, I think.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese contrasts a thought he had entertained—becoming a pond snail and living thoughtlessly—with his current sense that being human again might be acceptable. The English uses concessive 'even if' for a real past thought, stacks 'maybe,' 'would,' 'if,' and 'I think,' and turns 'having nothing to think about' into lacking any ability or object for thought.
ghs.remedy: I had considered being reincarnated as a pond snail and living without a thought in my head, but now I think becoming human again might not be so bad.

highlights.text: And so even if I had this idea of wanting to reincarnate into a pond snail and live my life without having anything to think about at all, maybe it would just be nice if I were to be a human again, I think.

ghs.en: Taichi: "Hahah..."

rows.jp: 頭痛と熱でもう。
rows.en: The headache and the fever had already…

ghs.en: The headache and the heat, by now,

rows.jp: 俺はいろいろな幻覚を見た。
rows.en: I saw one hallucination after another.

ghs.en: are making me see all sorts of illusions.

rows.jp: 自覚できないうわごとを発した。
rows.en: I babbled without even knowing it.

ghs.en: I fired off into ramblings, incapable of self-awareness.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that he uttered delirious words without being aware of them. 'Fired off into ramblings' combines incompatible phrasal constructions, while the trailing adjective says Taichi generally lacks self-awareness rather than that the speech is unconscious.
ghs.remedy: I babbled deliriously without even realizing it.

highlights.text: I fired off into ramblings, incapable of self-awareness.

rows.jp: 熱に翻弄される。
rows.en: The fever had me in its grip.

ghs.en: The heat makes sport of me.

rows.jp: 脳がとける。

ghs.en: The brain melts.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese refers to Taichi's own brain. English requires a possessive rather than the generic definite article.
ghs.remedy: My brain melts.

highlights.text: The brain melts.

rows.jp: だけど最後に俺は少しだけ―――
rows.en: But at the very end, just a little—

ghs.en: But at last, I will, just a little---
ghs.assessment: The source begins a final, immediate fragment about what Taichi does or experiences a little at the end. The English shifts it into future tense and isolates the verb from its absent complement with two commas.
ghs.remedy: But at the very end, I, just a little—

highlights.text: But at last, I will, just a little---
